tex_content.html:
Corollary
[$W^{1,2}$ solutions satisfy the global gradient estimate] 1. ch8:8.35\group ch08-generalized-solutions Under the hypotheses of Theorem 8.33, if $u\in W^{1,2}(\Omega )$ solves (8.83) and $u-\varphi \in W_0^{1,2}(\Omega )$, then $u\in C^{1,\alpha }(\overline\Omega )$ and satisfies (8.87).
Proof

\sketch Theorem 8.16 first bounds $u$. For a sufficiently large $\sigma >0$, Theorem 8.34 solves the shifted equation $(L-\sigma )v=g+D_if^i-\sigma u$ in $C^{1,\alpha }$. Uniqueness for the shifted problem gives $v=u$, and Theorem 8.33 applies.

□
